review_notes: Reviewed all 130 lines of TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialOrthogonalGroup/Center.lean. Checked the statements of all four declarations against the relevant definitions and lemmas: Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup and mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean, Subgroup.mem_center_iff in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Subgroup/Center.lean, IsRegular in Mathlib/Algebra/Regular/Defs.lean, scalar/scalar_apply/scalar_commute in Mathlib/Data/Matrix/Basic.lean, coordinateRotation and coordinateHalfTurn in TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialOrthogonalGroup/CoordinateRotation.lean, and TauCeti.sq_eq_one_of_smul_one_mem_orthogonalGroup in TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/OrthogonalGroup/Basic.lean. Also inspected the downstream uses in TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/Center.lean and TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/StandardComodule.lean. The hypotheses 3 ≤ Fintype.card n and IsRegular (2 : R) are jointly satisfiable (for example R = ℤ and n = Fin 3), so the main statements are not vacuous. The centralizer argument via coordinate half-turns and coordinate rotations correctly forces off-diagonal entries to vanish and diagonal entries to agree; the forward direction of mem_center_iff correctly derives c^2 = 1 from orthogonality and c^(card n) = 1 from the determinant, and the reverse direction uses the true fact that a scalar special orthogonal matrix is central. The extra conjuncts c^2 = 1 and c^Fintype.card n = 1 are automatic for g ∈ specialOrthogonalGroup n R (when n is nonempty), but they match the documented characterization of scalar orthogonal matrices of determinant one and are harmless rather than vacuous. I found no false, empty-domain, or misleading statement warranting a rubric finding. I could not execute Lean, so this review is based on source inspection only.
